title: Acceptance and invited method
summary: Acceptance is the offeree’s manifestation of agreement in the manner invited or required by an offer while the power to accept remains open.
notes:
First identify the offer and the invited response: a return promise, performance, or either. Then ask what the offeree did, whether that act communicated agreement or otherwise met the prescribed method, and when it became effective. Wucherpfennig distinguishes readiness to proceed from a present acceptance. International Filter separates executive approval from notice of approval. White examines work that did not communicate acceptance. For goods transactions, the UCC alters some common-law rules concerning the form of acceptance and nonmatching terms.

An offer may request a return promise, completed performance, or conduct capable of expressing commitment. First identify what the offer asks for; then identify the alleged responsive act and any notice requirement. Wucherpfennig finds further negotiations, International Filter finds a stipulated approval, White finds insufficient communicative preparation, and Ever-Tite finds commencement expressly invited by the form.
